data.gender_notes: Revathi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Goddess of the Moon who is also known as Chandra Mata or Revati. Revathi is a name that is filled with grace and beauty. It is a name that inspires a sense of wonder and mystery. The name Revathi carries the meaning “Moon Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Revathi usually hope their child will grow to embody moon goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Revathi is a name that signifies the divine power of the Moon. It is a name that represents femininity, nurturing, and protection. The name is believed to bring good fortune and prosperity to those who bear it.
data.etymology: Revathi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon Goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Revathi total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: In Hinduism, the moon god is an ancient and important deity. The moon is considered to represent knowledge, powers of illumination and fertility. In Indian astrology, the position of the moon at the time of one's birth is believed to significantly influence a person's character and destiny. Thus, the name Revathi, derived from the moon goddess, holds cultural significance as a name associated with knowledge, light, and the divine power of the moon.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Revathi has deep spiritual significance as it is connected to Chandra Mata, the Hindu goddess of the moon. In Hindu mythology, Chandra Mata is revered as the protector of knowledge, the giver of wisdom, and the source of all illumination. Thus, the name Revathi carries the blessings of the goddess of knowledge and wisdom, inspiring the holder of this name to seek knowledge, wisdom, and enlightenment in all aspects of their life. It also represents the divine power of the moon and the connection to the divine feminine energy.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Revathi, meaning 'the one who bestows grace and protection', embodies the divine nurturing energy of the universe. It symbolizes the endless flow of love and compassion, granting peace and tranquility to those who bear this name.

vedic_reference.note: There is no clear connection to Vedic texts or mythology for the name Revathi.

historical_references.reference: Revathi was a famous ancient poet and playwright in Sanskrit language during the Gupta Empire in the 5th century AD. He is known for his works in various genres, including drama, poetry and poetic dramas.
historical_references.context: Gupta Empire, Sanskrit language, poet and playwright

historical_references.reference: Another Revathi, a Jain monk and scholar, lived during the 11th century AD in the Deccan region of India. He is known for his works on Jainism, including commentaries on the Agamas and the works on grammar and logic.
